world.name: Go
world.title: Go: The Relay Guild
world.subtitle: Train at the Outpost, cross the Signal Tower, and build a relay that can survive a failed job.

paths.name: The Outpost
paths.description: Learn Go by turning recruit and supply records into reliable commands. Start with values and finish at a JSON boundary.
paths.topics: Bindings, types, functions, errors, control flow, slices, maps, structs, methods and JSON

paths.name: The Signal Tower
paths.description: Build the relay services once you can read Go functions and collections. Test contracts, coordinate workers, and reason about cancellation and ownership.
paths.topics: Interfaces, error wrapping, table tests, channels, context, generics and a bounded dispatch pool

paths.name: Full Relay Expedition
paths.description: Follow every guild mission in order, from making a first badge to dispatching concurrent work and preserving every result.
paths.topics: The full Go route from first programs through the worker-pool capstone

quests.objective: Compile a first Go program and use declarations, zero values and string operations.
quests.boss_brief: Implement badge(raw string) string. Trim leading and trailing whitespace, then uppercase the result. badge("  Jo \t") should return "JO". A whitespace-only input returns the empty string.
quests.side_quest: Print len("é") and the value from a range loop over the same string. Explain the difference.
quests.hint1: The strings package contains TrimSpace and ToUpper.
quests.hint2: Pass the result of strings.TrimSpace(raw) to strings.ToUpper.
quests.debrief: Use strings.TrimSpace before uppercasing, then return the resulting string. Try an all-whitespace name to check the boundary.

quests.objective: Return a value and an error, and branch before using a failed result.
quests.boss_brief: Implement parseCount(raw string) (int, error). Trim outer whitespace, parse a decimal int, and reject negative values. Return zero with a non-nil error for an invalid, overflowing, or negative input. Zero and positive counts succeed.
quests.side_quest: Compare parseCount("+2") with parseCount("2.0") and trace which inputs reach the domain check.
quests.hint2: Return early on a parse error. Use fmt.Errorf or errors.New when a parsed count is negative.
quests.debrief: Try empty text, zero, a negative number, and more digits than int can represent. Each test exercises a different rule.

quests.objective: Apply switch, loops, and early returns to a guard that can stop scanning.
quests.boss_brief: Implement isReady(states []string) bool. Return true when every state is exactly "ready". Return false for any other state. The empty slice counts as ready.
quests.side_quest: Add a separate function that returns the index of the first state that blocks departure. Choose a clear representation for no match.
quests.hint2: Return false as soon as state differs from "ready". Return true after the loop.
quests.debrief: The post-loop return covers both an empty slice and a slice containing only ready states. Put an invalid state in the middle to check the early exit.

quests.objective: Predict when slice operations share storage and make an independent copy on purpose.
quests.boss_brief: Implement withTag(tags []string, tag string) []string. Return a slice containing the original tags followed by tag. The result must have its own storage, including when the input has spare capacity. An empty input produces a one-element result.
quests.side_quest: Append to stock[:1:1] and explain what the third index changes. Compare the result with editing front[0] before the append.
quests.hint1: Allocate a slice of length len(tags)+1.
quests.hint2: Copy tags into the new slice and assign tag at index len(tags).
quests.debrief: Check the result with an input made using make([]string, 1, 3). Mutate result[0] afterward and verify the input is unaffected.

quests.objective: Count values in a map and distinguish missing entries from zero-valued entries.
quests.boss_brief: Implement tally(items []string) map[string]int. Return a non-nil map of exact string counts. Ignore empty strings. Preserve case and whitespace in every other key. A nil input gives an empty map.
quests.side_quest: Add a display helper that lists counts in descending order with alphabetic tie-breaking.
quests.hint1: Initialize a result map and range over items.
quests.hint2: Skip the empty string with continue. Update other keys with counts[item]++.
quests.debrief: Verify that "rope" and "Rope" occupy separate entries. Use the map's keys and values in tests so iteration order is irrelevant.

quests.objective: Model a hero with a struct and choose value or pointer receivers deliberately.
quests.boss_brief: Implement NewHero(raw string) (Hero, error). Trim the name, reject it if empty, and return Hero{Name: cleaned, XP: 0} on success. Return the zero Hero and a non-nil error on failure.
quests.side_quest: Copy a Hero with a slice of tags. Change a tag through the copy and trace why the original can see it.
quests.hint1: Use strings.TrimSpace to normalize the name.
quests.hint2: Return Hero{} with an error for an empty name. Otherwise the keyed literal can omit XP because its zero value is 0.
quests.debrief: Try a name with internal spaces. Trimming preserves the middle of a name while removing accidental padding.

quests.objective: Decode external data into a Go struct and validate the resulting values.
quests.boss_brief: Implement decodeHero(raw string) (Hero, error). Decode one JSON object, trim the name, and reject blank names or negative XP. Missing XP is accepted as zero. Return Hero{} and a non-nil error on failure. Unknown fields are allowed.
quests.side_quest: Change XP to *int and compare an omitted xp field, an explicit null, and a numeric zero.
quests.hint1: Declare var h Hero and pass &h to json.Unmarshal.
quests.hint2: Trim h.Name and reject an empty name or an XP value below zero after decoding succeeds.
quests.debrief: Use malformed JSON, valid JSON with the wrong XP type, and valid JSON with negative XP to exercise separate failures.

quests.objective: Accept the behavior a function needs and reason about method sets and nil.
quests.boss_brief: Implement ReadName(r io.Reader) (string, error) for a non-nil reader with bounded input. Read to EOF, trim outer whitespace, and reject an empty result. Return an empty string and a non-nil error if the read fails or the name is blank.
quests.side_quest: Define a reader whose Read method has a pointer receiver. Write a compile-time assertion using var _ io.Reader = (*YourReader)(nil).

route_choices.label: Continue
route_choices.reason: A Gate Error With a Trail

quests.hint1: Use io.ReadAll, then check its error before converting the bytes to a string.
quests.hint2: After trimming, return errors.New for an empty name. Test success with strings.NewReader.
quests.debrief: Use a reader that returns an error to check propagation separately from blank input. io.ReadAll is suitable here because the caller supplies bounded input.

quests.mission_title: A Gate Error With a Trail
quests.objective: Wrap an error with context while preserving the failure a caller can inspect.
quests.boss_brief: Implement openGate(name string, hasKey bool) error. Return nil if hasKey is true. Otherwise return an error whose message contains name and that matches the provided ErrSealed under errors.Is.
quests.side_quest: Define a GateError struct that stores a gate name, implements Error and Unwrap, and can be inspected with errors.As. With Go 1.26 or newer, try errors.AsType[*GateError] if you used a pointer receiver.
quests.hint1: Return early with nil when the key is present.
quests.hint2: Use fmt.Errorf with %s for the gate name and %w for ErrSealed.
quests.debrief: Check the message and errors.Is separately. Replacing %w with %v would preserve the text and lose the wrapped sentinel.

quests.objective: Translate a function contract into named table-driven tests.
quests.boss_brief: Implement clamp(value, low, high int) (int, error). Return 0 and a non-nil error when low exceeds high. Otherwise return the value limited to the inclusive interval with a nil error. Add a table-driven test in clamp_test.go locally.
quests.side_quest: Write a fuzz test that verifies a valid clamp result is between the bounds and stays unchanged when clamped again.
quests.hint1: Test low > high before applying either boundary.
quests.hint2: For each table row include whether an error is expected. Compare the result only when its value is part of the contract.
quests.debrief: Add cases with equal bounds and negative values. Change the function deliberately to return the input unchanged and check that the table catches it.

quests.objective: Send work over a channel, drain the values, and close from the producer side.
quests.boss_brief: Implement squareAll(nums []int) []int. Start one goroutine that sends the squares of nums over a channel and closes it. Collect the squares in input order. Return an empty slice for empty input. Assume every square fits in int.
quests.side_quest: Replace the output channel with a buffer of size one and trace which sends can complete before the receiver runs.
quests.hint1: Create the channel before starting the goroutine. Close it from the sender when the loop finishes.
quests.hint2: Range over the channel in squareAll and append each received value.
quests.debrief: Try an empty slice. The sender must still close the channel so the receiver can finish. A consumer that stops early needs a way to tell the producer to exit.

quests.objective: Carry cancellation through a blocking operation and handle channel closure separately.
quests.boss_brief: Implement waitForRune(ctx context.Context, signals <-chan string) (string, error). Return ctx.Err for an already canceled context. Otherwise wait for a signal or ctx.Done. Return io.EOF if the signal channel closes without a value, and allow the empty string as a successful signal.
quests.side_quest: Build a signal producer that selects on ctx.Done as well as its send. Check that stopping the consumer also allows the producer to exit.
quests.hint1: Check ctx.Err at entry, then select between ctx.Done() and a receive from signals.
quests.hint2: Use signal, ok := <-signals to distinguish a real empty signal from a closed and drained channel.
quests.debrief: Test with a buffered signal, a closed channel, and a canceled context. A canceled context can be constructed without any sleep.

quests.objective: Use type parameters when the same collection algorithm works across element types.
quests.boss_brief: Implement mapValues[T, U any](items []T, transform func(T) U) []U. Transform each item once in input order and return a fresh slice. Return a non-nil empty slice for a nil or empty input. Assume transform is non-nil.
quests.side_quest: Write a generic frequency function and explain why its key parameter needs comparable.
quests.hint1: Allocate make([]U, len(items)) and use range to get each index and item.
quests.hint2: Assign transform(item) to the matching output index.
quests.debrief: Test an int-to-string transform and a struct-to-bool transform. The same function should compile for both sets of types.

quests.objective: Bound active work, collect a result for each job, and keep stable input positions.
quests.boss_brief: Implement dispatch(jobs []func() (int, error), limit int) ([]Result, error). Reject limit below 1 even when there are no jobs. Assume all jobs are non-nil and return normally. Run every job exactly once with at most limit active. Preserve both job return values in input order and continue after a job error. Return a non-nil empty slice for no jobs with a valid limit.
quests.side_quest: Add context-aware jobs and define a result for each unstarted index. Decide when cancellation should stop the sender and what happens to in-flight jobs.
quests.hint1: Allocate the results and start min(limit, len(jobs)) workers. Send indices through a channel.
quests.hint2: Each worker loops over indices. After sending every index, close the channel and wait before returning results.
quests.debrief: Use blocking test jobs to control completion order and track the peak active count. Include a failing job and verify that a later job still runs.
